idea: Self-attention computes to_q/to_k/to_v from the same input, so the three weight matrices stack into one [3*inner, K] GEMM. Each output row keeps its full K reduction, so the arithmetic per element is unchanged, but the GEMM shape changes and the kernel may change with it. Exactness therefore has to be measured, not assumed.
key_finding: The small 2048-wide projections at 26 tokens were running at about 186 GB/s against a 537 GB/s roofline. Fused they reach roughly 569 GB/s -- a 3.0x speedup on those layers, and bitwise exact.
design: Fuse only where the fusion is exact at every shape that module actually sees. The audio and cross projections at 26 tokens qualify and give 2.3-3.1x. The video projections are already at roofline (1.04x at 64 tokens) and are NOT exact at 256, so they stay unfused -- no shape-conditional numerics are needed.
still_to_test: audio cross k/v at the real text-context length
v2a k/v at 64 and 256 video tokens
the same fusions with the real checkpoint weights rather than random ones
limitations: synthetic weights of the checkpoint shapes, isolated GEMMs, not in-model
a fused weight is a second copy unless the originals are released, so the placement and memory accounting must be redone
no clip-level result; the four-tensor oracle remains the authority
